title: Interception of registration and device-enrollment data in transit
description: Account registration details and camera/sensor enrollment data sent from the Homeowner to the Home Hub could reveal directly identifying information such as name, email, phone number, account identifiers, device serial numbers, or network identifiers if observed on the communication path.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may traverse a local network or setup channel where confidentiality protections could be weak or misconfigured during onboarding.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure/eavesdropping of data in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Linkability via persistent identifiers and metadata on the flow
description: Persistent account identifiers, device IDs, MAC addresses, serial numbers, or repeated enrollment traffic patterns on this flow could allow an observer to link multiple setup actions to the same household or homeowner, even if payload contents are partly protected.
assumptions: Assumes enrollment exchanges expose stable identifiers or recognizable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability from identifiers/metadata in transit; exact node id may vary.

title: Detectability of home-security system setup activity
description: The mere presence, timing, frequency, or size of registration and device-enrollment messages may let an observer detect that a smart-home security system is being installed or expanded at a specific residence.
assumptions: Assumes a network observer can see traffic metadata even if content is encrypted.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability from communication metadata; exact node id may differ.

title: Linking homeowner identity with enrolled devices at the Home Hub
description: On receipt, the Home Hub can associate the homeowner's account identity with specific cameras and sensors, creating a consolidated profile of the household and its installed monitoring equipment.
assumptions: Assumes the hub stores account and device enrollment records together or under a common account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side linking of datasets/identifiers; exact node id may vary.

title: Identification of the homeowner from registration data
description: The Home Hub receives registration information that may directly identify the homeowner or make them identifiable when combined with device and household context.
assumptions: Assumes registration includes direct identifiers or sufficient quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side identification from received data; exact node id may vary.

title: Inference of household occupancy and security posture from enrolled devices
description: By processing the set of enrolled cameras and sensors, the Home Hub can infer sensitive facts such as home layout coverage, likely occupancy patterns, entry points being monitored, and the household's security concerns.
assumptions: Assumes the hub processes or stores device types, locations, or configuration details.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-fit inference/profiling-style disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for secondary use of registration and enrollment data
description: The Homeowner may not be adequately informed, or may lack meaningful choice, regarding how the Home Hub or its ecosystem will use account and device-enrollment data beyond setup, such as analytics, service improvement, or sharing with vendors/cloud services.
assumptions: Assumes notices/choices may be incomplete or bundled during onboarding.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance around notice/consent; exact node id may vary.

title: Unawareness of what personal and household data is captured during onboarding
description: During registration and enrollment, the Homeowner may be unaware of the full scope of data collected by the Home Hub, including device identifiers, network details, household configuration, and account metadata.
assumptions: Assumes onboarding UX does not clearly explain data collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Lack of evidence about homeowner consent or enrollment actions
description: If the Home Hub does not maintain trustworthy records of what the Homeowner registered or enrolled, and under what notice/consent conditions, the homeowner may later be unable to prove or dispute those actions, and the system may be unable to demonstrate compliant handling.
assumptions: Assumes onboarding actions and consent events are not logged with integrity protections.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability gaps; exact node id may vary.

title: Interception of temporary access code in transit
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be observed or captured while being transmitted from the guest-facing input path to the Home Hub logic, allowing identification of the guest or association of the guest with a specific visit or property access event.
assumptions: Assumes the code entry traverses a communicative path or interface that can be monitored, such as a wireless keypad, mobile-to-hub channel, or exposed internal bus rather than being purely local and physically shielded.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for interception/eavesdropping may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated guest access attempts
description: Metadata on this flow, such as timing, source interface characteristics, or repeated use of the same temporary code, could allow an observer to link multiple unlock attempts to the same guest or household visit pattern.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can access flow metadata or the code is reused across multiple entries.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat is grounded mainly in metadata-based linkability on the flow.

title: Detectability of guest presence from unlock-code submission
description: The mere occurrence of this flow may reveal that a guest is physically present at the home and attempting entry, even if the code content is protected.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker can observe network traffic, keypad activity, RF emissions, or other side channels correlated with code submission.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact detectability subtree may vary.

description: Upon receiving the temporary access code, the Home Hub may map the code to a specific guest identity or profile, thereby identifying the individual who is entering.

uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended as identification through received credentials.

title: Linking guest visits over time at the Home Hub

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact linkability subtree may differ.

title: Guest cannot plausibly deny code submission

uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended as non-repudiation caused by logging of the submission.
